source_pages: printed p.221-223 / PDF 223-225. p.221 read 2026-08-20; p.222 and p.223 read 2026-08-23 and verified against 170-dpi renders. Everything except the two corner types.
family_naming_note: Namespaced 'Wall H.60' for the same reason as 'Wall H.36': the registry merges section files by family NAME, and the catalog uses 'H. 60' for both a base family and a wall family. The catalog's own wording is preserved in 'section'.
extraction_note: COMPLETED 2026-08-23 except the corners. The original note said compound units were left out because they 'carry internal partitions' - that reading was wrong and is kept here rather than erased (learned rule 9). A compound carries ONE door across two or three carcass modules, so the envelope and the front are both ordinary; the modules are an interior fact and travel as modules_mm. wall_h48.json established that the same day and this section follows it. STILL OUT: the straight corner PD094D/S and the 90-degree corner OD0713 / OD0715, both gated on Elda Q7b.
letter_note: PD = H.60 was CONFIRMED from factory estimate 2026/30829 (PD0631) BEFORE this page was opened, and the page now agrees: PD0631, W.60, d.35, H.60. That is the order in which the two sources arrived, and it is worth remembering - the estimate named a letter no page we had read could have given us.

data.mounting_note: Catalog-level fact: every unit in the wall chapter hangs. HOW HIGH it hangs is not in the catalog and is not here - the generator takes it from Standards::WALL_MOUNT_BOTTOM_MM, a project default awaiting M1.6, and writes it onto the object as mount_bottom_mm (Contract v1.5).
data.n_elle_note: The second elevation on this page is labelled 'N- Elle' at 62,2 = H + 2,2, the same +22 mm seen at H.36 (38,2), H.72 (74,2) and H.84 (86,2). N_Elle is its own chapter, printed p.321. RECORDED, NOT IMPLEMENTED. CORRECTION 2026-08-23, evening (learned rule 9 - added, not erased): THIS FIGURE IS NOT PRINTED ON THE PAGE. pdftotext -bbox puts 'N- Elle' at a normal 7,5 pt over the perspective drawing on every wall page of this chapter; rendering exactly that box at 400 and at 600 dpi shows blank paper. It is white text, or a hidden layer for the N_Elle edition - IN THE FILE, NOT IN THE BOOK. The wording above ('the elevation carries', 'the second elevation on this page') is therefore wrong, and the H.48 note's guess that the 170-dpi render merely lacked resolution is wrong too. THE NUMBER STAYS, RELABELLED: a document lead BELOW source trust, used for nothing and not to be quoted to Elda as something the catalog prints. Learned rule 10 says the render is the page; this is the first time the text layer claimed something the page does not, and it will not be the last.
page_observations: THIS PAGE IS THE FIRST WALL PAGE WITH A SIDE-HINGED DOOR. printed p.211 (H.36) had none, which is why the printed p.11 five-centimetre closing-strip rule did not bite there. It bites here: PD0131, PD0531 and PD0631 are 'rh or lh' doors, so a run that puts one against a tall unit or a wall, with a 'D' handle, wants a closing strip of at least 5 cm. Warn, never auto-insert.

THERE IS NO PULL-OUT DOOR TYPE ON THIS PAGE. H.72 and H.84 both open with one (PE0130 / PG0130 at W.15); H.60 does not. The W.15 slot here is PD0131, an ordinary door. One more reason the suffix cannot be decoded across families.
THE WIDTH SET OF THE ONE-DOOR TYPE IS 15 / 45 / 60 - there is no W.30, although H.72 and H.84 both list one. Widths are per type per family, read from the row.
Suffix 30 appears exactly once on this page, at W.90, and means TWO DOORS. Suffix 31 means ONE door. At H.72 the same 30 means a pull-out door at W.15 and two doors at W.60/W.90.

wall_door.description: Wall unit with door - 1 rh or lh door - 1 shelf
wall_door.notes: ONE CODE, BOTH HANDS - and for once this is not a reading, it is CONFIRMED. Factory estimate 2026/30829 orders PD0631 with OPENING DIRECTION: Left (rows 15, 25) and with Right (rows 18, 27). The hand is an order variant carried on the line, never a second article. Anything that splits one of these into an rh code and an lh code is wrong, and tools/test_contract.rb fails if it happens.

wall_top_hung_door.description: Wall unit with top-hung door - 1 top-hung door - 1 shelf
wall_top_hung_door.notes: Same width set and same suffix 00 as the H.36 top-hung type, which is a coincidence of this pair of pages and not a rule. The page lists Servo Drive mechanism 554 and Power adapter 224 as surcharges with NO article code - not recorded as companion_refs, because a companion is resolved from the registry and never typed. Open for Elda (Q8).

front_layout.note: One door covering the full front, hinged along its top edge - the mirror of the bottom-hung figure, plan rectangle identical.

wall_push_up_door.description: Wall unit with push-up door - 1 push-up door - 1 shelf - interior Valencia handle - no Push-pull device
wall_push_up_door.notes: Extracted as DATA with no opening symbol, decided 2026-08-20. A push-up door is not hinged, so the Drawing_Spec hinge-axis rule does not describe it and there is no honest figure yet. front_layout therefore carries a mechanism and NO hinge_axis, which is exactly how base_pull_out_door is handled on printed p.36: 70_symbols draws a leaf only when it is told an axis, so an unwritten rule draws NOTHING rather than something wrong. The convention is a task of its own, not a blocker on the codes. The page also lists Valencia handle 23, Servo Drive mechanism 554 and Power adapter 224 as surcharges without article codes.

front_layout.note: One full-front leaf carried by a push-up mechanism. NO hinge_axis: no elevation V is ever drawn for this type. What IS drawn is open_leaf below - the front itself, dashed, where it ends up. NOTE THE SYSTEM DIFFERS FROM H.36: printed p.560 calls H.36/H.48 VERTICAL and p.561 calls H.60/H.72 OBLIQUE. Same word on the unit page, two different motions.

open_leaf.frame: y from the FRONT FACE (negative = in front of it), z from the CARCASS BASE. Both mm. The two entries are the leaf's long edges; the slab is swept across the full unit width and thickened on its outer face.
open_leaf.source_ref: printed p.561 / PDF 563, 'Oblique push-up door system h. 60'
open_leaf.note: OBLIQUE system: the leaf tips outward. Printed 82 / 25,4 / 18 with a 60 leaf close with NO residue - 82 - 25,4 = 56,6 of run, drop = sqrt(60^2 - 56,6^2) = 19,9, giving a length of 60,0. The PICTURE draws the leaf at 32,8 degrees; the NUMBERS give 19,4. The numbers win, which is the same rule that governs the corner hand. The upper edge lands 96 mm INSIDE the cabinet footprint - not visible in the picture at all.

wall_compound_2_push_up.description: Compound wall unit with push-up door - 1 push-up door - 2 shelves - interior Valencia handle - no Push-pull device
wall_compound_2_push_up.notes: THE COMPOUND PUSH-UP IS NOT THE SAME ARTICLE FROM FAMILY TO FAMILY. H.48 offers exactly ONE, PC1808 at 180 wide in 90+90; H.60 offers TWO, at 90 in 45+45 and 120 in 60+60, and no 180 at all. Different widths, different splits, and even the suffix differs from the dish-drainer twins. Read the row. NOTE ALSO: this is the only position on printed p.222-223 with NO prohibition block at all - no symbol, no finish names - while its H.48 counterpart carries a full one.

front_layout.note: One push-up door across both modules. NO hinge_axis - see wall_push_up_door, which also carries the printed open_leaf geometry for this family's OBLIQUE system. Not repeated here: the page gives the mechanism once, for the simple type.
